title: Release audit: README.md still documents `.../v0.1.0/install.sh` for the install command and fo
summary: Update both documented commands to the current release installer (v0.1.1 or a versionless latest URL) and add a README guard test that asserts the install and uninstall commands use the release installer.
requirements: R1: README.md contains no reference to the `v0.1.0` install script URL (`.../v0.1.0/install.sh`), in the install command or anywhere else.
R2: The README install command and the README uninstall command reference exactly the same install-script URL, and that URL is the only install-script URL in README.md.

R3: The install-script URL in README.md points at the release whose behavior the documentation describes (the current release, i.e. the v0.1.1 release referenced by the audit finding), not at an earlier tag. The version selector appears exactly once in the URL and both commands inherit it.
R4: No other README content changes: the surrounding prose, command shape (`curl -fsSL <url> | bash`), options and section structure stay as they are, except for the URL itself.

R5: If the chosen URL names a release tag that is not yet published at commit time, the README names the newest published tag instead and the discrepancy is recorded in the task report; README must never advertise a tag that does not resolve.

R6: The existing test suite passes, and tests/test_readme_install.py either already fails on the stale URL (and therefore now passes) or is extended to assert R1 and R2 without weakening any existing assertion.
R7: No change to install.sh, forge_code/*, pyproject.toml or the release directories is introduced by this task.
acceptance: A1: A grep for `v0.1.0/install.sh` in README.md returns nothing.
A2: All install-script URLs found in README.md are identical, and there are at least two of them (one in the install command, one in the uninstall command).
A3: The version selector in the README install-script URL equals the version documented as the current release, and the URL is fetchable (HTTP 200) from the public repository.
A4: The README diff contains only URL changes, reviewable as a small, self-contained change.
A5: `python -m pytest` passes for the whole repository, including tests/test_readme_install.py.
A6: `git diff --name-only` lists only README.md and, optionally, tests/test_readme_install.py.
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

checks.criterion: AC1. README.md's first install command is exactly the canonical versionless command.
AC2. The update and uninstall commands use the canonical URL, the uninstall line carrying `-s -- --uninstall`.
AC3. README.md contains no tag-pinned install-script path.
command: if grep -nE '/v[0-9][^[:space:]/]*/install\.sh' README.md; then exit 1; fi

checks.criterion: AC4. The canonical URL returns HTTP 200 and serves the installer.
AC5. The guard errors on a tag-pinned path, on divergent URLs and on another branch's URL, each via assertRaises.
AC6. The guard imports no network module and passes without network access.
AC7. The README documentation test in tests/test_cli.py asserts the canonical versionless URL.
AC9. The task commit contains exactly README.md, tests/test_readme_install.py and tests/test_cli.py.
command: import subprocess,sys; out=subprocess.run(['git','show','--name-only','--format=','HEAD'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout; got=sorted(p for p in out.split() if p); sys.exit(0 if got==sorted(['README.md','tests/test_readme_install.py','tests/test_cli.py']) else 1)

external_dependencies.name: GitHub raw content host (raw.githubusercontent.com)
external_dependencies.interface: HTTPS GET of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh returns HTTP 200 and the body of the POSIX `sh` installer; the same path pattern `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<org>/<repo>/<ref>/<path>` is what the guard rejects when `<ref>` is a release tag.

external_dependencies.name: curl
external_dependencies.interface: `curl -fsSL <url>` streams a URL body to stdout for `sh`; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' <url>` prints the HTTP status code used by the AC4 check.

result.summary: README.md now documents exactly one install-script URL — the versionless canonical `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh` — in the install, update and uninstall commands; the three v0.1.1 URL substitutions from the previous session stand, tag-pinned paths are gone, and the surrounding prose, command shape (`curl -fsSL <url> | sh`, `| sh -s -- --uninstall`), options and section structure are untouched. tests/test_readme_install.py keeps the text-only canonical-URL guard (`assert_single_install_script_url`) which rejects a stale `v0.1.0` install-script path, any `/v<tag>/install.sh` path, fewer than two install-script URLs and any URL other than the single canonical string, with the negative cases proven through `assertRaises`/guard raising only (`test_stale_install_script_url_is_rejected`, `test_divergent_install_script_url_is_rejected`, `test_another_branch_install_script_url_is_rejected`, `test_a_missing_install_script_url_is_rejected`, `test_rejects_a_stale_url_anywhere_in_the_document`); the module imports only `re`, `unittest` and `pathlib`, so no network module and no network access. tests/test_cli.py's ReadmeTest asserts the canonical versionless URL through `INSTALL_URL` and rejects any `/v<tag>/install.sh` path without forbidding the default branch. A CHANGELOG.md entry written by an earlier attempt was reverted to its committed content (the file is now byte-identical to HEAD) because the specification forbids a changelog change and its entry names the v0.1.1 release. Verified by `python -m pytest -q`: 214 passed, 137 subtests passed. install.sh and tests/test_install.py remain pre-existing unrelated worktree modifications and tests/test_check_cleanup.py remains untracked; none of them is part of this change set.; the completion step could not decide which uncommitted files belong to the task
assumptions: The repository default branch is `main`, so the canonical versionless installer URL is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh`; the specification's Assumptions section states the same.

The v0.1.1 tag the specification names is not published (`git for-each-ref refs/tags` shows no tags), so the versionless default-branch URL is used and no release version is named next to the commands.
AC4 (HTTP 200 for the canonical URL) was verified in an earlier session by a direct HTTPS GET that returned 200; this session's command policy rejects `curl`, so the check could not be repeated here.
CHANGELOG.md is left exactly as committed: the specification excludes a changelog change and its [Unreleased] section already records the README fix.
The commit itself is performed by the runtime; the change set offered for it is README.md, tests/test_readme_install.py and tests/test_cli.py only.

last_failure.message: The specification is internally contradictory and incomplete on this tree. (1) A6 and Scope Boundaries restrict the diff to README.md and, optionally, tests/test_readme_install.py, and list 'Changing CHANGELOG.md' as out of scope, while A5 requires the full suite to pass; tests/test_cli.py's ReadmeTest asserts the literal `raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh` and a companion test rejects a default-branch install URL, so A5 cannot hold unless tests/test_cli.py is edited. Three rework rounds failed on exactly this point. (2) The spec never enumerates the exact committed file set, so the completion step cannot decide which uncommitted files belong to the task. (3) The spec ignores that the worktree already contains unrelated modifications (install.sh, tests/test_install.py, untracked tests/test_check_cleanup.py) that belong to another task and must stay uncommitted. (4) The spec assumes the coder commits (`git commit -s`) although this agent's git is read-only, so the runtime must stage and commit only the named files. Required rewrite for v3: state the committed change set explicitly as README.md, tests/test_readme_install.py and tests/test_cli.py, and decide CHANGELOG.md explicitly (either add it to the allowed set as a documentation-consistency file or forbid it outright) so A6, the non-goals and A5 agree; require the versionless canonical URL `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/main/install.sh` in all install-script command lines; require the guard in tests/test_readme_install.py to prove its negative cases via assertRaises with no network imports; state that install.sh, tests/test_install.py and tests/test_check_cleanup.py are pre-existing unrelated changes that must remain unstaged and are excluded from the completion comparison; state that the runtime performs the commit and that the acceptance check `git diff --name-only`/`git show --stat HEAD` is evaluated only over the named set; and keep A2/A3 (no `v0.1.0/install.sh`, canonical URL fetchable with HTTP 200) unchanged.

result.last_summary: README.md now documents one install-script URL, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh, in the `## Install` command, the `### Update` command and the `### Uninstall` command (`| sh -s -- --uninstall`); the only README change is the URL in those lines, so no `.../v0.1.0/install.sh` reference remains. tests/test_cli.py's `ReadmeTest::test_readme_has_a_pinned_install_command` now pins the full v0.1.1 command instead of the v0.1.0 URL. CHANGELOG.md keeps exactly one English `## [Unreleased]` bullet recording the fix. tests/test_readme_install.py keeps the text-only guard built from the single `INSTALL_TAG = "v0.1.1"` constant and gains the two named rejection tests required by the spec: `test_stale_install_script_url_is_rejected` feeds the guard's own `assert_single_install_script_url` a document carrying `/v0.1.0/install.sh`, and `test_divergent_install_script_url_is_rejected` feeds it a document whose second install-script URL names another tag; both require the same assertion the positive path uses to raise, so the guard is proven by behaviour rather than message wording. The module imports only `re`, `unittest` and `pathlib` and fetches nothing. Verified with `python -m unittest -v tests.test_readme_install tests.test_cli.ReadmeTest` (37 tests OK) and the full `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (211 tests OK, ~141 s). Note: the documented installer URL currently answers HTTP 404 because the v0.1.1 tag is not published yet; that is recorded under spec_issues.; uncommitted files outside the contract: install.sh, tests/test_check_cleanup.py, tests/test_install.py
